full_judgment:
24. Finally, the learned Advocate cited the case of Moulvi Ali Gohar Vs. The Crown reported in 1969 SC MR 501 for the purpose of showing that the burden of proof lies on the prosecution and if it fails to prove its case the benefit of doubt must be given to the accused. 

 "The burden of the prosecution to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt never shifts, and whether that burden has been discharged or not should be decided on the case as a whole and if in dealing with the whole case, a reasonable doubt arises then the benefit of that doubt must be given to the accused and he must be acquitted though what he has pleaded has not been fully established by him."
